claims.text: Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind defined in helm/helm pkg/release/v1/util/kind_sorter.go, and chart authors cannot declare dependencies between resources or subcharts except through hook weights.
Pulumi derives resource ordering from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready, and independent resources deploy in parallel.
The Helm docs state: "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's kind_sorter is a hardcoded list of Kubernetes kinds beginning with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with unlisted kinds (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the same kind-order list in reverse.
Helm sends the sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and does not wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
Helm chart dependencies do not change ordering: a subchart's objects are merged into the parent chart's set and sorted by kind.
Helm chart hooks ordered with helm.sh/hook-weight annotations are resources Helm doesn't manage as part of the release.
Native sequencing for resources and subcharts has been proposed in HIP-0025, which is still a draft.

Passing one resource's output into another or setting the dependsOn resource option creates an edge in Pulumi's dependency graph; the Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to be ready before creating dependents; deletes follow the graph in reverse.
helm.v4.Chart supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering between objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for dependencies on outside resources.
Pulumi's parallel deployment of independent resources makes updates faster than a strict serial sequence.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of Pulumi and Helm together.
There are three common ways to adopt Pulumi alongside or in place of Helm.
Using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program is the most common adoption pattern.
helm.v4.Chart resources show every child in plan output, drift detection, and state.
Helm merges objects from a chart and all dependencies into a single set, sorts by Kubernetes kind, and applies in that order, so declaring a subchart as a dependency doesn't make it install first.
Pulumi installs the chart after the resources it depends on when outputs are passed into chart values.
Helm records each install or upgrade as a numbered release revision and helm rollback restores a prior revision.
